original.reason: The argument assumes every neighborhood contains an open interval (a,b) with endpoints in X. This fails for basic neighborhoods at a minimum or maximum, which are rays/half-open intervals.

judgment.reason: Its one-sided case incorrectly suggests (a,x] has closure in [a,x] and then asserts [a,x] is contained in (a,b), although a is not in (a,b). The ray cases are also not established.
The treatment of basic rays is false/incomplete: absence of an interior point on the finite-endpoint side need not make the ray a singleton; it may contain points on the other side.
The crucial shrinking fact, especially for rays and one-sided endpoint cases, is only asserted rather than proved. It also does not establish T1 if regularity is taken in the standard T1 sense.
Its ray argument wrongly states that if there is no interior point on the finite side then the ray is a singleton; a basic ray can still contain points on its other side.
